key_insight: CRISP turns stable probability rankings into robust spatial priors, enabling source-only medical image segmentation that remains reliable under domain shift without test-time updates or target data.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the reliability of automated segmentation when models are deployed across hospitals, patient groups, or imaging modalities that differ from training data.
method: Uses the assumption that positive-region ranking is stable under shift.
Creates high-precision (HP) and high-recall (HR) priors via latent feature perturbations.
Iteratively refines these priors during training to squeeze them toward the final mask.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on multi-center cardiac MRI and CT lung vessel segmentation, with reported HD95 reductions of up to 0.14, 1.90, and 8.39 pixels across multi-center, demographic, and modality shifts.
watch_item: Performance depends on the validity of the rank-stability assumption, which may not hold for all anatomy, scanners, or severe distribution shifts.
paper_title: CRISP: Constrained Refinement via Iterative Squeezing Process for Robust Medical Image Segmentation under Domain Shift
